newsitem.title: USA: NBA-RODMAN OUT REST OF SEASON, MAY BE BACK FOR PLAYOFFS.
newsitem.headline: NBA-RODMAN OUT REST OF SEASON, MAY BE BACK FOR PLAYOFFS.

text.p: Dennis Rodman of the Chicago Bulls sprained a ligament in his left knee on Tuesday and likely will miss the rest of the regular NBA season, a Bulls' spokesman said on Wednesday.
Rodman will "be in a brace the next couple of days and we'll limit his activities," Bulls General Manager Jerry Krause said in a radio interview over WBBM.

"Then we'll start on therapy a couple of days from now. He'll be in a brace and on crutches. We're going to take every precaution with it. Darn thing, with two seconds to go in the game last night of all freak things. We expect him back for the playoffs."
Rodman, 35, sustained the injury on Tuesday when he banged knees with Mavericks forward A.C. Green on a rebound in Chicago's 94-92 victory.

The Bulls lead the league with 60-9 record so far this season. They won an NBA-record 72 games last season, but their chances of winning 70 games for the second straight year will be reduced without Rodman.
Rodman is leading the league in rebounding again this season, pulling down 16.1 boards a game.
But his play off the court made more spectacular headlines.
Earlier this season, he was hit with an 11-game suspension for kicking a cameraman and later was kept out of a game for slapping Milwaukee Bucks forward Joe Wolf in the groin.

Rodman began his career with Detroit in 1986 and helped the Pistons win consecutive titles in 1989 and 1990. He was named NBA Defensive Player of the Year in 1990 and 1991 and won the first of his five rebounding titles in 1992.
He is the only player in history to win a major statistical category with three different teams.
